title: Why Cortés Fired His Spanish Surgeons: Aztec Obsidian, Agave & Bone Nails

teenKit.tldr: When conquistador Hernán Cortés faced catastrophic head and limb injuries in 1520, Spanish medical care meant probing dirty wounds with rusted iron and pouring boiling oil into them. Meanwhile, Aztec medicine used ultra-sharp volcanic glass and antiseptic plant saps that were lightyears ahead of medieval Europe.
teenKit.whyItMatters: It proves that advanced science and high-level engineering existed outside of Europe long before Western colonizers realized how much they had to learn from indigenous cultures.
keyTakeaways: Pachuca obsidian blades split at a molecular level, creating a cutting edge only 3 nanometers thick—far sharper than any modern steel surgical scalpel.
Aztec wound care utilized hyperosmolar agave sap, which naturally sucked moisture out of bacteria to prevent lethal infections without chemical burns.
Surgeons in the Florentine Codex documented complex procedures like using pine and bone pegs to stabilize shattered bone fragments inside the body.

vocab.meaning: A severe head injury where a portion of the skull is broken and pushed inward, pressing directly against the brain tissue.
A solution property that draws water out of bacterial cells through osmosis, effectively dehydrating and killing the infection.

quiz.question: Why did 16th-century European battlefield surgeons pour boiling oil into open wounds?
options: To sterilize the wound tissue of dirt
To neutralize what they mistakenly believed was poison from gunpowder
To numb the pain through thermal shock
quiz.explanation: European doctors operated on the bizarre superstition that battlefield wounds were inherently poisoned, causing them to torture patients with boiling oil.

quiz.question: What makes Pachuca obsidian uniquely suited for ancient surgery?
options: It naturally contains antibiotic properties that fight off tetanus
It fractures down to a 3-nanometer edge, making it sharper than modern steel
It melts slightly under body heat to seal incisions shut
It glows under ultraviolet light to reveal hidden bacteria
quiz.explanation: Obsidian breaks along molecular lines to form an edge thousands of times thinner than a human hair, causing microscopic tissue damage compared to metal.

quiz.question: What was the primary function of agave sap in Mexica trauma care?
options: It acted as a heavy structural glue to hold shattered skulls together
It created a hyperosmolar environment that dehydrated and killed bacteria
It numbed the central nervous system like modern medical cocaine
It dyed the skin so doctors could track the spread of internal bleeding
quiz.explanation: The concentrated sap created high osmotic pressure, sucking water straight out of invading microbes and stopping infections before they started.
